fixes.explanation: That's the word. Verse 116 says, "Sustain me as You promised, that I may live; let me not be ashamed of my hope." He's asking the LORD to hold him up, and he ties that request to what God promised. The thing he doesn't want to be ashamed of is his hope.
That's it, friend. Verse 97 says, "Oh, how I love Your law! All day long it is my meditation." Not a quick visit and not a drive-by. The whole day is his time with God's law.

A sunrise start sounds lovely, but the psalm doesn't say that. Verse 97 says, "All day long it is my meditation." So he doesn't clock out once the morning is over. His thoughts keep going back to God's law the whole day.

One hour is a nice habit, but it isn't what the psalm says. Verse 97 says, "All day long it is my meditation." That's way more than an hour's worth of love. He keeps God's law in his thoughts from start to finish.

Yes, ma'am, yes, sir, that's what it says. Verse 99 says, "I have more insight than all my teachers, for Your testimonies are my meditation." He gives the reason right in the verse. His insight comes from thinking on God's testimonies.

You got it, baker. Verse 104 says, "I gain understanding from Your precepts; therefore I hate every false way." Notice the "therefore." The understanding comes first, and the hatred of false ways follows from it.

That's the picture. Verse 105 says, "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path." A lamp for your feet is about seeing where you're walking. Anybody who's crossed a dark room knows how much a little light helps.

Not quite. Verse 112 says, "I have inclined my heart to perform Your statutes, even to the very end." Nothing in the verse says "until my troubles are over." He says he has inclined his heart to perform them to the very end.

That's right. Verse 112 says, "I have inclined my heart to perform Your statutes, even to the very end." The verse doesn't tie it to his troubles ending. He says he has inclined his heart to perform them to the very end.

Yes, that's false. Verse 114 says, "You are my hiding place and my shield; I put my hope in Your word." The verse names what he puts his hope in, and it's God's word. His own strength isn't mentioned.
The verse doesn't mention his name. Verse 116 says, "Sustain me as You promised, that I may live; let me not be ashamed of my hope." The word is hope.

This one is true, so let's read it again. Verse 118 says, "You reject all who stray from Your statutes, for their deceitfulness is in vain." The psalmist says God rejects those who stray, and he gives the reason. Their deceitfulness is in vain, which means it's empty.
